chapter_theme: The second fifth of the Puranamalai turns from what the poet failed to see to what the Fullness is: after a run of stanzas on the weariness of being born (mother, kin, Brahma and the fire are all tired of him, eighty-four lakh births), the refrain of failure gives way to a litany of the Lord's forms, as seed and shape, as guru, kundalini, Sakti, nada and bindu, as light and dark, as the three channels, as body and life, as every kin and all seven orders of beings, as male, female and neuter. Caste is one creation of his, the body a pot of filth, and the poet's whole claim is that he did not know the one who was all of this.
structure_note: 699 and 706 are the only petitions (புகலருள்வாய், வரமருள்வாய்); 699 to 702 share the word அலுத்தேன் (grew weary) and build to the count of births; from 716 the stanzas take a new shape, a chain of ஆய்/ஆகி participles listing the forms the Lord took, closed by அறியேன் (I do not know), which runs on through chapter 41.

699.reading: The mother grew weary of bearing and the poet weary of being born; he asks the Fullness to give its golden feet and grant him refuge.
699.nuance: பெற்றலுத்தாள், she grew weary of bearing, is the mother of many births, not one; பொற்றுணைத்தாள், the golden pair of feet, is the refuge asked instead of another womb. The stanza is the first petition in the work after twenty-five confessions.

700.reading: Kin grew weary of weeping, the mourners of burning him, the mother of bearing him, and the poet of being born.
700.nuance: Four parties are tired: the weepers, the burners, the mother, the born. உறன்முறையார், those of the proper relation, are the kin whose office it is to cremate; the stanza makes a whole lifetime out of the two ceremonies that bracket it, and 701 extends the weariness to the gods.

701.reading: Brahma grew weary of creating, the poet of being born and dying, and the strong fire of consuming him.
701.nuance: The creator and the cremation fire (அக்கினி) are made as tired of the cycle as the one in it; the stanza's wit is that even the agents of birth and death want it to stop. உரமுடைய அக்கினி, the strong fire, has eaten him many times.

702.reading: Born through eighty-four lakh births and wounded by them, the poet says he lamented.
702.nuance: எண்பத்து நான்கு நூறாயிரம், eighty-four lakh, is the traditional count of the kinds of birth (as in Tirumanthiram 409), here taken as the count of the poet's own births. புண்பட்டு, wounded, is the only word for what the births did.

703.reading: While you were within me, not knowing myself and not knowing you, the poet says he lost the body.
703.nuance: Two not-knowings are set side by side, of oneself and of the Lord, and the Lord's being within (எனக்குள்ளே) makes them one failure. உடல் இழந்தேன், lost the body, is the ordinary death read as waste: the body was the place of the meeting that did not happen.

704.reading: The poet says he does not know how you, mingled as embryo and form and become the whole world, stood formless.
704.nuance: கருவாய் உருவாய், as seed and as shape, and then அருவாகி, becoming formless: the stanza holds the Lord as the embryo, its body, every world and no form at once, the first of the chapter's litanies of forms. The confession shifts from பாராமல் (not seeing) to அறிகிலேன் (not knowing).

705.reading: Not praising the holy feet in the red-gold lotus, the poet says he became a ghoul that dances when the drum is beaten.
705.nuance: செம்பொற்கமலம் may be a lotus of red gold, the Lord's feet themselves, or the crown lotus of the yogic body where the feet are placed; the verse does not fix it. பம்பை கொட்ட ஆடும் பசாசு, the ghoul that dances to the drum, is the possessed dancer of folk exorcism, a self that moves only as it is beaten.

706.reading: You being within me and I within you, the poet asks for the boon that ends the mind's distress.
706.nuance: The mutual indwelling (எனக்குள் நீ, உனக்குள் நான்) is stated as a fact and the boon asked on its strength; Sivavakkiyar (971) asks the same formula as a question. மனக்கவலை, the mind's distress, is the one thing the poet asks to have removed.

707.reading: Not seeing faultlessly the one who stood within the seven kinds of beings and played, the poet says he lost his use.
707.nuance: எழுவகைத் தோற்றம், the seven kinds of beings, is the Tamil count of the orders of life (gods, men, beasts, birds, crawling things, water creatures, plants), which 722 lists in full. விளையாடினது, played, is the Lord's sport in all of them.

708.reading: Not able to know the differences of caste for what they are, the poet says he stood deluded by habit.
708.nuance: சாதிபேதங்கள் தனை அறியமாட்டாமல் may mean not knowing what caste distinctions really are (empty, as 709 says) or not knowing them in the ordinary sense; 709 settles it toward the first. வாதனை is the Sanskrit vasana, the residual impression of past deeds, so the delusion comes from habit laid down in earlier births.

709.reading: Not knowing that you created lineage as one, the poet says he stood deluded inside the pot of filth.
709.nuance: குலம் ஒன்றாய் நீ படைத்த குறை is hard: குறை may be the point or the lack, so either 'the point that you made all lineage one' or 'the flaw in your making lineage one'; the first fits 708 and the Siddhars' general view. மலபாண்டம், the pot of filth, is the body, and the argument is Sivavakkiyar's: bodies of one stuff cannot differ by caste.

710.reading: The poet says he does not know the sign of the form you took, as atom within atom, in all the cosmos and the body.
710.nuance: அண்டபிண்டம் is the Siddhars' compound for the universe and the body as one; அணுவுக்கு அணுவாக, atom to the atom, makes the Fullness the smallest thing in both. குறிப்பு, the sign or intent, is what the verse says cannot be read.

711.reading: Not praising the true guru who sits above the thousand-petalled lotus, the poet says his understanding was lost through the anava of the inner self.
711.nuance: சகஸ்திரம், the thousand, is the crown lotus, and the guru placed above it is the Lord as guru rather than a human teacher, as tradition reads it. ஆணவம் is the first of the three impurities in Siddhanta, the soul's self-assertion; the verse makes it the one cause of not seeing.

712.reading: Not subduing the five senses and praising you, the poet says he wore away, melted and his heart trembled.
712.nuance: ஐந்து பொறியை அடக்கி, subduing the five senses, is set as the condition of praise, the Kural's tortoise (126) made the Siddhar's first step. The second line repeats 678's trembling.

713.reading: You made me dance this way as your holy dance; not knowing you, the poet says his body was wasted.
713.nuance: ஆட்டுவித்தாய், you made me dance, makes the poet's whole life the Lord's dance, with the poet as the puppet; the complaint is not that he was danced but that he did not know the dancer. திருக்கூத்து, the holy dance, is thus moved from the hall to a single life.

714.reading: Inside the stench of sinew, flesh, skin and bone, not able to know the limit, the poet says he was deluded.
714.nuance: The body is four tissues and a smell; வரம்பு, the limit or bound, is unexplained, and may be the body's own end, the measure of conduct, or the boundary between the body and the one inside it (684, 696). The stanza's pairing of the inventory with delusion is the Naladiyar's (46).

715.reading: Not seeing the good that was within the living creature, like a spider's thread, the poet says he lost his good.
715.nuance: சிலந்தியுடை நூல் போல், like the spider's thread, is a simile whose point is not stated: the thread is fine and easily missed, or it is spun from the spider's own body as the world is from the Lord, the Upanishadic image. நலம், the good, is both what was in the creature and what the poet lost, a pun the chapter uses often.

716.reading: The poet says he does not know how you, as guru, becoming the Supreme, as kundalini, Sakti, nada and bindu, became formless and formed.
716.nuance: குடிலை is the Agamic name of the primal power, the kundalini (kutila, the coiled); the chain குரு, பரம், குடிலை, சத்தி, நாதம், விந்து runs down the order of manifestation in Tirumular's cosmology (382, 384), with the guru placed first. Whether the guru here is the Lord or a man the verse does not say.

717.reading: The poet says he does not know the breadth of you who stood as light, as sun and moon, as the dark within, as fire, and became space.
717.nuance: The three lights (sun, moon, fire) and the dark are all the Lord, with உள்ளிருள், the inner darkness, named alongside the lights as his form; வெளி, space, is where the list ends, as the ascent of chapter 39 ended at உச்சி வெளி. கதிர் மதி is also cipher for the two channels, so the list may be read of the body too.

718.reading: The poet says he does not know the measure of you who stood as ida and pingala and as the suzhumunai that rose, as body and as life.
718.nuance: The three channels are named outright and the Lord is identified with them, not placed in them; எழுந்த சுழுமுனை, the whirl-channel that rose, is the middle channel the Siddhars prize, called risen because the breath rises in it. உளவு, the measure or secret, is what is unknown.

719.reading: The poet says he does not know the reckoning by which you stood as the root seed, sprouted and stayed in every body, and then destroy it as Kaalan.
719.nuance: மூலவித்து, the root seed, is the Lord as the origin of each body, which he then ends as Death (காலன்); creation and destruction are one agent, and கணக்கு, the reckoning, is the account by which he does both. The seed-and-sprout image recurs at 729 and 739.

720.reading: The poet says he did not know clearly that you were within the body, inside and outside at once.
720.nuance: உள்ளும் புறம்பும், inside and outside, undoes the chapter's own inside-outside argument: the Lord was not only within the body but outside it too, so the error was not of place but of clarity (தெள்ள).

721.reading: The poet says he does not know the state in which you stood as mother, father, kinsmen, relations and all the kin.
721.nuance: The kin that 686 called unreal are here the Lord's own forms; the two stanzas are not in conflict, since what was false was their lasting and what is true is who stood in them. தமர் and கிளைஞர் are the near and the wider kin.

722.reading: The poet says he does not know the intent with which you stood in the seven orders: beasts, birds, crawling things, the unmoving, the gods, the water-born and the human lines.
722.nuance: This is the full list behind 707's எழுவகை: விலங்கு, புள், ஊர்வன, அசரம் (the unmoving, plants), விண்ணவர், நீர்ச்சாதி, மனுக்குலம், seven in all. மனுக்குலங்கள், human lineages, is plural, so the human castes are one of the seven and not more.

723.reading: The poet says he does not know the manner in which you stood in glory, becoming male, female, neuter and other forms.
723.nuance: அலி, the neuter or hermaphrodite, is included among the Lord's forms without comment, and வேற்றுரு, other shape, leaves the list open. The verse says the Lord became these (ஆகி), where Tirumular (1872) says the inner light is none of them; the two can be reconciled by reading 'became' as 'appeared as', but the verse does not make the distinction.

links.note: 698 asks how many mothers and fathers the poet has been born to; 700 adds the other parties to each birth, the kin who weep and the relations who burn the body, and says all of them, with the mother, are weary of it.

Both give the count of eighty-four lakh (எண்பத்து நான்கு நூறாயிரம்). Tirumular says the Lord spreads as life through the eighty-four lakh kinds; Pattinathar says he was born through eighty-four lakh births and wounded. The kinds of birth in the one are the poet's own births in the other.

Sivavakkiyar asks how it is that you are within me and I within you (எனக்குள் நீ உனக்குள் நான் இருக்குமாறு எங்ஙனே); Pattinathar uses the same words as a settled fact (எனக்குள்ளே நீயிருக்க உனக்குள்ளே நானிருக்க) and asks a boon on its strength. The formula is the same; one poet wonders at it, the other builds a petition on it.

Sivavakkiyar asks what caste is, when all water is water, the elements are one and all ornaments are one gold; Pattinathar says the Lord created lineage as one and that he stood deluded inside the pot of filth. Both deny caste any ground in the body's stuff; Sivavakkiyar argues it, Pattinathar confesses it as a thing he failed to know.

Kakapusundar says we have no caste or clan, my clan is the clan of seed, and all lives were born alike in Brahman at the first; Pattinathar says the Lord made lineage one and the body is a pot of filth. Both ground the denial of caste in the one origin of all bodies; Kakapusundar names the seed, Pattinathar the filth.

Agasthiyar says the cosmos becomes the body (அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும்) and sets the self in the atom-space; Pattinathar says the Lord took form atom within atom in all the cosmos and the body (அண்டபிண்டம்). Both hold the universe and the body as one field and the smallest thing as the Lord's place; Agasthiyar makes it a truth to become, Pattinathar a sign he could not read.

Sivavakkiyar says that to hold within oneself the measureless light that is atom and cosmos (அணுவினோடும் அண்டமாய்) is release; Pattinathar says the Lord is atom within atom in cosmos and body and that he did not know the sign of that form. The pairing of the atom with the whole is the same; Sivavakkiyar makes seeing it release, Pattinathar not seeing it his loss.

Kakapusundar says the one Brahman became an endless dance in the world, as good and evil, sun and moon, hills, creeping things and the marks called guru and disciple; Pattinathar brings the dance down to one life, 'you made me dance this way as your holy dance', and makes his not knowing the dancer the loss. The cosmic dance of the one becomes the poet's own being danced.

The Naladiyar lists entrails, fat, blood, bone, sinews, skin and flesh and asks which part is the garlanded woman; Pattinathar lists sinew, flesh, skin and bone and their stench and says that inside them he was deluded. Both make the inventory of tissues the cure for delusion about a body; the Naladiyar aims it at desire for another's body, Pattinathar at his own.

Tirumular's spider sits at the centre of its web and feeds on what it catches, as the master sits in the house of the five senses and consumes the five objects; Pattinathar's spider is only a thread, the good within the living creature that he failed to see. The spider is the same creature in both; the point is the spider's feeding in the one and its fine thread in the other.

Tirumular says that in nada is bindu and in nada and bindu Siva and Shakti come within, and that knowledge and action are born as they divide; Pattinathar lists the Lord as guru, Supreme, kundalini, Sakti, nada and bindu, formless and formed. The sequence of Shakti, nada and bindu as stages of the Lord's manifestation is the same; Pattinathar adds the guru at its head.

Tirumular says all the kalas run in ida and pingala and the unnamed middle channel, and rousing the base to the head one reaches the holy feet; Pattinathar names ida, pingala and the risen suzhumunai and says the Lord stood as them and as body and life. Both hold the three channels as the frame of the practice; Tirumular leaves the middle one unnamed, Pattinathar names it and makes it the Lord.

Sivavakkiyar says the one that was first became forms upon forms, rose as caste differences and became every living being; Pattinathar lists the seven orders of beings, with the human lineages as one of them, as forms the Lord stood in. Both make the one the source of all the kinds of life, with caste or lineage counted among those kinds rather than above them.

Tirumular says the light within the dark is neither woman nor man nor neuter (பெண்ணல்ல ஆணல்ல பேடல்ல) and cannot be known by anyone; Pattinathar says the Lord stood in glory becoming male, female, neuter and other forms (ஆணாகிப் பெண்ணாய் அலியாகி). On the reading that 723's ஆகி asserts that the Lord is these forms, the two make opposite claims about the same three; on the reading that he only appears as them, Tirumular's denial stands and the verses agree.

source_issues: 711 breaks its first line in mid-word, போற்றாம / லகத்தினுடைய, so that the line division of the print falls inside போற்றாமல்; the text itself is sound.
716 and 717 have internal sandhi that the printing leaves joined (நாதவிந்தாய், இருளாயக்கினியாய் for இருளாய் அக்கினியாய்); not errors, but the words must be cut by the reader.
